title: Practice question
description: One question. In a .jsonl file each line is one of these objects; in a .json file the top level is an array of them. Programming types (fill_blank, find_fix) and conceptual types (multiple_choice, calculation, param_count, open_ended) share the common fields but use different content fields - see the 'allOf' rules at the bottom.

id.description: Unique across ALL question files. e.g. 'lin-reg-train-loop-01'.

type.description: fill_blank / find_fix: programming. multiple_choice: closed question with options. calculation: free numeric answer(s) (loss values, output shapes, ...). param_count: like calculation but about trainable-parameter / weight counts. open_ended: free text, self-graded against a model answer.

category.description: Category / provenance used by the filter UI: the script file for programming questions (e.g. '01_linear_regression.py') or the source document for the other types (e.g. 'GeneralAssignment3.md', 'Quiz1A_reference_solution.pdf'). Use the exact same string for every question from the same file.

item.description: Where in a source document the question comes from, e.g. 'Question 12' or 'Part II.2'.

description.description: Programming types only. 1-3 sentences: what the (correct) snippet does overall and why. Always shown to the learner. Must NOT leak the answer.

code.description: Programming types: Python source, lines separated by \n (fill_blank: contains <<BLANK:id>> markers; find_fix: the BUGGY code). Other types: optional supporting material shown in a code block under the prompt - a model definition, a matrix, a shape table. Must NOT contain <<BLANK:...>> markers.

hints.description: Ordered from vague to specific. Revealed one at a time. The last hint may be nearly the answer. Required for programming types, optional for the others.

explanation.description: Shown after checking / revealing. Programming types: optional, why the answer is what it is. multiple_choice / calculation / param_count / open_ended: REQUIRED - the full reasoning (why the correct answer is right and, for multiple_choice, why the others are wrong; or the worked calculation).

related_reference.description: Names of entries (see reference.schema.json 'name') that help with this question. Shown as chips that open the reference panel.

prompt.description: Non-programming types: the question text. Plain text; `inline code`, **bold**, $inline LaTeX$ and $$display LaTeX$$ (KaTeX) are rendered. In JSON, double every LaTeX backslash (\times, \frac). A blank line starts a new paragraph.

selection.description: multiple_choice only. 'single': exactly one option is correct (radio buttons). 'multiple': one or more are correct (check boxes); graded all-or-nothing, like the quizzes.

options.description: multiple_choice only. Shown in this order, labelled A, B, C... by position. Never refer to other options by letter in any text.

text.description: The option as the learner sees it. `inline code` allowed.

explanation.description: REQUIRED for every option. Correct option: why it is right. Incorrect option: the specific reason it is wrong (the misconception, or the true fact) - never just 'this is wrong'.

parts.description: calculation / param_count only. One numeric answer box per entry.

label.description: What this box asks for, e.g. 'in_features' or 'Total trainable parameters'. Required when there is more than one part.

tolerance.description: Accepted absolute error. Default 0 = exact (use for counts and shapes). For decimals set e.g. 0.005 when 2 decimals are expected.

unit.description: Optional text shown after the input, e.g. 'parameters'.

model_answer.description: open_ended only. A complete, concise reference answer (2-6 sentences).

key_points.description: open_ended only. The checklist a good answer must hit; the learner ticks the ones they covered when self-grading.

blanks.description: fill_blank only. One entry per <<BLANK:id>> marker in 'code'.

answers.description: Every accepted answer. answers[0] is the canonical one shown as the solution. Multi-line answers use \n.

accepted_patterns.description: Optional extra regexes (JS syntax, implicitly anchored ^...$) tested against the learner's input after trimming and collapsing whitespace runs to one space. Use only when listing every answer is impractical.

placeholder.description: Optional greyed-out hint text inside the input, e.g. 'optimizer step'.

multiline.description: Force a multi-line text area. Defaults to true when any answer contains \n.

errors.description: find_fix only. One entry per buggy line in 'code'.

fixes.description: Every accepted replacement for that line (leading indentation is ignored). fixes[0] is canonical. Use "" to accept deleting the line.

explanation.description: What is wrong with this line.
